messages:
Maya Patel: noticing a spike in 5xx from the hosted inference infra starting ~08:12 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~8% on the gateway. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/inq (plots attached).
Eli Chen: seeing timeouts at our gateway layer too, mainly 504s and some 502s. Latency p50 -> p99 increased. Any recent deploys?
DeployBot: canary deploy started: rollout/rl-serve-v2 -> 10% traffic @ 08:05 UTC (triggered by ci/cd pipeline).
Sasha Rivera: @maya which config changed in that canary? I reviewed the PR earlier; there was an auth-header canonicalization flag and a change to retry backoff.
Maya Patel: yes, feature flag `normalize_auth_header` toggled true in canary (intended to fix inconsistent client headers). It rewrites Authorization -> Bearer <token> style.
Tom Nguyen: logs show many upstreams returning 401 -> followed immediately by 5xx from our gateway due to a panic in the auth middleware when header parsing fails. Sample stacktrace: ```panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range\n/infra/auth/parse.go:87```
Priya Kumar: ugh. That middleware is shared by hosted inference route and dedicated endpoints. Can confirm error surfaces in /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
Eli Chen: we also have an increase in billing-reported failed requests from customers (webhooks show 502s). Support already has tickets from two enterprise customers.
Support Bot: Created support ticket #4521 and escalated to SRE. Customer snippet: "requests failing with 502, intermittent auth errors".
Sasha Rivera: this is a bad canary then — parsing change causing panics for certain legacy auth header formats. Need rollback or quick patch. How fast can we remove the flag?
Maya Patel: I can flip the runtime flag in the control plane immediately, but the canary instances might still be serving until the rollout completes or is rolled back.
Tom Nguyen: If we flip the flag off in feature flags, the config reload should avoid the panic. But the canary binary still contains the code path; safe to toggle? We tested flag gating before but maybe code path still invoked during init.
Eli Chen: charting error traces: frequency of panic logs lines up exactly with canary start. Containg nodes: rl-serve-v2-canary-*.
Maya Patel: executing admin API: `POST /admin/flags/normalize_auth_header false` now.
DeployBot: feature flag update acknowledged by control plane @ 08:18 UTC.
Tom Nguyen: checking pod logs for reload. Hmm some pods still showing panic. Looks like the reload didn't reach init-time path; stack shows parse invoked during request handling though.
Priya Kumar: can we shift traffic away from canary instances at the ingress? We should throttle to 0% for that rollout instead of waiting for normal rollback.
Eli Chen: ingress supports weight override. I'm going to set rollout weight to 0 for the canary group: `curl -X POST https://router/admin/route -d '{"route":"rl-serve-v2","weight_canary":0}'`
Eli Chen: done @ 08:23 UTC. Traffic to canary dropped to ~0%. Error rate trending down but still above baseline due to in-flight requests and instances still returning errors.
Sasha Rivera: alerting customers: Support, can you patch customer-facing status and recommend retry/backoff?
Support Bot: Draft message: "We are investigating increased 502/504 errors for the hosted inference API. No data loss; recommend clients retry with exponential backoff. We'll update in 30 minutes." Approving?
Maya Patel: approve. Post it and add link to incident slack.
Support Bot: Status update posted to status.redwood at 08:28 UTC.
Tom Nguyen: I can repro locally by sending edge-case auth header `Authorization: Bearer` (no token) and a trailing space; parse code is assuming token length > 1. Repro steps: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer " https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` Response: server panics -> 502.
Priya Kumar: good repro. Create quick patch: guard parse for empty token and return 401 instead of panicking. Can we hotfix on canary and prod?
Maya Patel: hotfix requires build + deploy; takes ~15-20m. Flipping flag and routing away should be faster. I think proceed with routing override + feature flag flip.
Eli Chen: agree. We also need to coordinate rollback in the CI to ensure canary is marked failed and not promoted.
Sasha Rivera: starting formal incident timeline: detection 08:12, suspected cause canary auth parse 08:16, feature flag flip 08:18, route weight override 08:23, mitigation in progress.
Tom Nguyen: I'll still prepare the patch PR: `fix(auth): guard empty token parsing` and tag for expedited review.
Maya Patel: Ops, can we run a sweep to restart the failing canary pods after weight=0 to drain connections and stop panic logs?
Eli Chen: yes, I'll cordon and drain: `kubectl scale deployment rl-serve-v2-canary --replicas=0 -n inference` -> done @ 08:31 UTC. Pods terminating, in-flight requests draining.
Priya Kumar: metrics are back near baseline; 5xx reduced to ~0.9% at 08:35 UTC. Keep monitoring.
Support Bot: Customer ticket update sent to #4521: "We mitigated the issue by removing the canary from rotation; working on permanent fix. Please retry and let us know if you still see failures."
Sasha Rivera: who will own postmortem and RCA? Maya + Tom + Eli?
Maya Patel: I'll own the postmortem draft and coordinate with Tom (patch) and Eli (rollout controls).
Tom Nguyen: will push the hotfix PR and request merge after tests.
Eli Chen: action items: 1) confirm canary not promoted, 2) add CI gate preventing init-time parsing changes without fallback, 3) add metric alert for panic stacktrace frequency.
Maya Patel: timeline for rollback/close: If no regression seen for 60m, we can close incident and start RCA.
Priya Kumar: adding small note — we should inform sales execs for affected customers. @Support please send a proactive email.
Support Bot: Email template posted in #support-ops.
Sasha Rivera: closing comment: good catch and quick routing override saved us. Let's document lessons: feature flags must guard both init and request-time code paths; canary weight override should be the default mitigation for mid-deploy regressions.
Maya Patel: thanks team. Will post full RCA within 48h.
IncidentBot: incident status -> mitigated at 08:40 UTC; monitoring for 1h."
